scenes.line1: Can threads see each other's changes?
scenes.say: Can threads see each other's changes? Why does it matter for thread safety?

scenes.label: Atomic
scenes.sub: Atomic operations finish in one step, preventing races.
scenes.say: Atomic operations finish in one step, preventing race conditions between threads.
If Thread A changes a value, Thread B may see old data unless you use synchronization to ensure memory visibility.
In Java, AtomicInteger's incrementAndGet is atomic. Volatile ensures memory visibility for shared variables.

scenes.question: Is volatile always thread safe?
scenes.right: No, volatile only ensures visibility. Atomicity needs atomic types or locks.
